//! The SAME wiring, made clean two ways: the production graph wires a REAL verifier through the
//! existing `with_verifier` seam, and the `Structural*` mock survives ONLY as a `#[cfg(test)]`
//! double (which the scanner admits — a test double is not the production graph).
use std::sync::Arc;

/// Production: wire the REAL OIDC verifier through the existing seam (no `Structural*` construction).
pub fn human_sso_app_spec(store: PrincipalStore) -> HumanSsoAuthenticator {
    HumanSsoAuthenticator::with_verifier(store, Arc::new(OidcCredentialVerifier::new(jwks)))
}

// The type DEFINITION + impl of the mock are fine — only CONSTRUCTION in prod trips the scanner.
pub struct StructuralVerifier;
impl StructuralVerifier {
    pub fn new() -> StructuralVerifier {
        StructuralVerifier
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    fn test_authenticator(store: PrincipalStore) -> HumanSsoAuthenticator {
        // `#[cfg(test)]`-gated: the mock is a TEST double, admitted.
        HumanSsoAuthenticator::with_verifier(store, Arc::new(StructuralVerifier::new()))
    }
}
